newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower in technical correction.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on profit taking, unaffected by news of U.S. missile attacks against Iraq, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 1.36 points, or 0.74 percent, to 182.66 on an all-share turnover of only 53 million shekels against 67 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 index fell 0.95 percent to 192.25.

"Everything today happened on a very low volume and the market was not reacting to events in Iraq. The market has been very strong in the last week and a technical correction had to come," said Jonathan Ross at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"Last week the market rose following insider share buying and the battles for controlling interests in several companies. Now that it's over the market is quiet," he said.

"The market was very sleepy today and activity was low. The markets abroad were also declining on fears that the Fed (U.S. Federal Reserve) might raise interest rates," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
He added that 194, where the Maof closed on Monday, was a key resistance level.

The most-active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.75 percent to 26,607 on volume of 3.1 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 0.25 percent to 115,012 on turnover of 2.9 million shekels.
Africa Israel Investments rose 2.25 percent to 494,475 on volume of 2.4 million shekels and traders said someone was trying to buy shares off the floor.
